result:
Solution 3's answer of 6 matches the exceptional graph as I recall it from the literature, the octahedron, which is the smallest simple connected planar 4-regular graph. I did not verify its case analysis in full. I only confirmed that the orientation it gives is Eulerian (every vertex has out-degree and in-degree 2) and uses all 12 edges.

Solution 1 names the square antiprism (8 vertices), but it gives no real argument, and it first tries to rule out the octahedron with a flawed claim. Solution 2 gives 50 vertices and a "Möbius strip" graph, which is unsupported guesswork.

VERDICT 1: REJECT
VERDICT 2: REJECT
VERDICT 3: ACCEPT
